minor_characters.name: Renner
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The Grand Dragon Lord's adviser who manages the Maiden selection ceremony and tries to direct Stephanie toward Xander before Miriam intervenes.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His function as ceremony-master can be folded into Xander or Blake's dialogue without losing any plot beat from the synopsis.

minor_characters.name: Darda's husband
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Briefly mentioned as the elderly male servant tangled in the bedsheet during Miriam's second escape attempt.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is unnamed, has no lines, and his presence adds nothing to the comedy of the scene that Darda alone cannot carry.

minor_characters.name: Galen
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The white-haired physician who tends to the poisoned Xander and explains that only the Lady's tears can cure silver-talon poison.
minor_characters.reason_removable: The synopsis names him but his role as exposition-deliverer could be merged with Apuleius or Cayden; however, since he IS named in the synopsis, he must be retained — excluded.

minor_characters.name: Jethro
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Cayden's elderly golden-cloaked priest who assists Apuleius in opening the Portal and compliments Stephanie.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He performs a ritual function that Apuleius alone could perform without altering the Portal demonstration or the ensuing attack.

minor_characters.name: The unnamed taxi driver
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Drives Miriam and Heather in the opening chapter's chase sequence and accepts cash to lose a tailing red car.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is a one-scene utility figure whose role can be compressed into a single line of action without losing the chase's function as menace foreshadowing.

minor_characters.name: The unnamed pig-men henchmen
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Blake's two nameless cohorts who help drug, abduct, and transport the women.
minor_characters.reason_removable: They are interchangeable muscle whose collective presence is preserved by retaining Blake; individuating them adds nothing.

subplots.name: Heather's matchmaking running gag
subplots.reason_removable: The repeated jokes about Heather setting Miriam up with creepy guys can be compressed to a single line establishing the Blake introduction without losing thematic content.

subplots.name: The killer-sheep demonstration
subplots.reason_removable: Stephanie's encounter with the aggressive wool-creatures is a self-contained worldbuilding aside that doesn't affect the Portal visit or the dragon attack that follows.

subplots.name: The northern-borderland raid intelligence
subplots.reason_removable: Xander's overheard conversation with Renner about scout reports and unknown northern dragons is foreshadowing for later books and not needed for Book 1's resolution.

digressions.topic: Extended worldbuilding on dragon biology, glands, mating scents, and the longevity of dragons
digressions.reason_removable: Much of the taxonomic exposition about dragon nature can be trimmed to the essentials the synopsis names (glands, scented mates, dual nature) without the extended Q&A.

digressions.topic: Detailed description of the Portal's vine-covered carved-dragon iconography and the century of magic used to build it
digressions.reason_removable: The ornate ritual description is atmospheric and can be condensed since the synopsis only requires the mirror-surface awakening and the stone-to-glass demonstration.

skippable_chapters.reason_removable: This is a sneak-peek excerpt from the next book that follows the resolution of Book 1 and contains no content the synopsis depends on.
